流星是星星掉下来了吗？: Is a meteor a falling star?
跟着一小块太空碎片，看看它进入大气时发生什么。: Follow a small piece of space debris and see what happens when it enters the atmosphere.
小碎片：途中完全消散: Small fragment: lost in the air
有一小块幸存落地: A small fragment survives to land
流星体：太空里的小碎片: Meteoroid: a small object in space
小碎片已经消散: The small fragment has been lost
剩下一块：不再明亮发光: A fragment remains: no bright glow
陨石：到达地面的碎片: Meteorite: a fragment on the ground
还在太空中，没有流星亮迹；它不是远处的恒星。: Still in space, with no meteor streak. It is not a distant star.
高速进入大气，与空气相互作用，产生亮迹，同时损失物质。: High-speed atmospheric entry produces light through interaction with air while material is lost.
这一条旅程没有陨石落地。小碎片在空中已经消散了。: No meteorite lands in this journey. The small fragment has been lost in the air.
幸存碎片已经减速，亮迹消失，还会继续下落。: The surviving fragment has slowed. Its bright trail is gone, but it continues falling.
幸存的碎片落地了，现在叫陨石。远处的恒星从来没有掉下来。: The surviving fragment has landed and is now a meteorite. The distant stars never fell.
先猜一猜，再动手试试: Make a guess, then try it
互动科学场景；操作和完整解释见下方: Interactive science scene; controls and full explanations follow below
慢慢玩 · 约 5—8 分钟: Explore at your pace · About 5–8 minutes
小碎片在太空里叫流星体。它高速进入大气，和空气相互作用，产生短暂的亮迹，我们把这: The small object in space is a meteoroid. When it enters the atmosphere at high speed, interaction with the air produces a brief luminous streak called a meteor. The distant stars are still there.
许多小流星体在空中就消散了。有些比较能撑住，会有一部分继续落到地面，剩下的那一块: Many small meteoroids are lost in the atmosphere. Some survive in part and reach the ground; the surviving piece is a meteorite. A meteor and a meteorite are different things.
先停在太空里：它有没有拖着亮尾巴？再把旅程推进到大气中。比较两种结尾：每一颗流星: Pause in space: is there a bright trail? Move into the atmosphere. Compare the two endings: does every meteor leave a meteorite?
高速进入大气时，流星体与气体碰撞并传递能量，周围气体及脱落物质可被加热、激发并发: During high-speed atmospheric entry, the meteoroid collides with gas and transfers energy. Surrounding gas and ablated material can be heated, excited and luminous, while the object ablates, fragments and slows. It is not simply friction followed by wood-like burning. A surviving fragment often slows into a dark-flight phase before reaching the ground.
两条路径是预先选定的教学情景，并非按大小预测结果的数值模拟。真正结局还受速度、入: The two paths are selected teaching scenarios, not numerical predictions from size. Real outcomes depend on speed, entry angle, density and structure. Height, atmospheric depth, object size, glow and time are not to scale; a dashed path remains for comparison. Meteorites do not always create large craters, and luminous flight need not continue to the ground.
路径、石块与时间均为示意: Path, rock size and time are illustrative
碎片穿过渐密的大气，发光、减速，并留下逐渐扩散的余迹: A fragment enters increasingly dense air, glows, slows down, and leaves a spreading wake
亮点跟着碎片向前，余迹留在经过的空气里，慢慢散开。碎片正在失去物质。: The bright head moves with the fragment. The wake remains in the air it passed through and slowly spreads. The fragment is losing material.
这一条旅程没有陨石落地。留下的余迹还会渐渐变淡，它不是继续飞行的石头。: No meteorite lands in this journey. The remaining wake fades; it is not a rock still flying onwards.
幸存碎片已经减速，不再明亮发光。它继续向下落，留在高处的余迹渐渐散去。: The surviving fragment has slowed and stopped glowing brightly. It keeps falling while the wake left higher up disperses.
先停在太空里，看看有没有亮尾巴。再看发光的一段：亮点向前走时，后面的余迹有没有一: Pause in space and look for a bright tail. Then watch the luminous stage: does the wake move onwards with the bright head? Compare both endings and look for a fragment that has stopped glowing.
亮头沿轨迹前进，尾后的发光气体和脱落物质留在经过的区域，逐渐扩散、受风扰动并改变: The luminous head advances along the path, while glowing gas and removed material remain in the region it crossed, spreading, responding to winds and changing brightness. Some meteors leave longer-lasting self-emitting trains, whose glow can also be sustained by atmospheric chemistry. A train is not simply a hot tail of rock attached to the head.
轨迹、减速、剩余物质和余迹扩散采用预设教学曲线，未求解气动力、烧蚀或大气化学。虚: Path, deceleration, remaining material and wake spreading follow prescribed teaching curves, without solving aerodynamics, ablation or atmospheric chemistry. The dashed line shows only the selected example’s path. Height, rock, glow and time are not to scale, and stage durations are adjusted. These examples have visible wakes; not every meteor leaves a persistent train. Real dark flight also depends on winds, shape and mass. This page cannot predict a meteorite’s landing location.
